newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-PENPIX OF WOMEN'S FINALISTS AT THE AUSTRALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PENPIX OF WOMEN'S FINALISTS AT THE AUSTRALIAN OPEN.

text.p: Portraits of Martina Hingis and Mary Pierce, who will contest the Australian Open women's final on Saturday:

The most exciting prospect in women's tennis since Monica Seles, she will become the youngest Grand Slam champion in the Open era if she beats Pierce. She will also move up to second in the world rankings, behind Germany's Steffi Graf, regardless of the result. She has not dropped a set in Melbourne. Despite her small frame she hits groundstrokes with intimidating power and accuracy, thanks to her split-second timing which allows her to take the ball on the rise. Her control of the racquet face allows her to project the ball at unexpected angles. Her speed around the court is unsurpassed in the women's game and she chases every ball.
Seeding: 4. Age: 16. Plays right-handed. Weight: 53 kg. Height: 1.67m. Ranking: 4. Tournament wins: 3. Career prize money: $1.6 million.

The tournament diva who wears her heart on her sleeve, former champion Pierce has shown new mental strength in recent weeks. She is still a crowd favourite in Melbourne after her 1995 victory -- fans love her aggressive, athletic game -- but she will need all the support she can muster to defeat Hingis. Pierce was born in Canada, plays for France and is based in the United States. After taking a three-month break from the game last year, she has come back more confident and relaxed. She believes maturity and experience have improved her game. A slow starter, she strikes the ball with brute power and enjoys coming into the net.
Seeding: unseeded. Age: 22. Plays right-handed. Weight: 61 kg. Height: 1.80m. Ranking: 22. Tournament wins: 7. Career prize money: $2.3 million.
